A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Simple Guidance Mechanisms for Discrete Diffusion Models. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-modeling and guided-generation experiments in Section 5, with additional ablations and generation results in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and results in Section 5 and the renumbered Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The D-CFG and D-CBG procedures in Section 3 and the UDLM objective and parameterization in Section 4 are retained. Appendix B supplies a theoretical CTMC correspondence without establishing a change to the proposed or implemented algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use Species10, QM9, CIFAR10, text8, Amazon Review, and LM1B, with the same language-modeling, guided-generation, and unconditional-generation tasks. No evaluated domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix comparisons, including FUDGE, PPLM, and NOS in the guidance experiments. The expanded discussion of Nisonoff et al. does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The data splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, sample counts, and guidance sweeps are retained. Experimental Details moves from Appendix C to D; the new theoretical Euler-sampling discussion does not revise an evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The continuous-time training ablation, guidance-strength sweeps, first-order approximation comparisons, and sampling-step analyses are unchanged. Appendix D becomes E, retaining the same supporting tables and Figures 4–6.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same five-seed generation experiments and mean ± standard deviation reporting, including Tables 4–5 and 15–33. No run-count disclosure or uncertainty-estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, rankings, plotted trends, and generated examples are unchanged across Tables 1–7 and 14–37 and Figures 2–6. The appendix renumbering introduces no additional empirical findings.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.1–B.2 adds substantial derivations claiming continuous-time equivalence between D-CFG/D-CBG and CTMC guidance, including Euler sampling and guided-rate formulas. The previous UDLM–CTMC and SEDD-bound derivations remain in Appendix C. The added reasoning contains inconsistencies as printed, notably Equation (41) and the product-to-sum substitution in B.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about discrete guidance, the UDLM continuous-time bound, small-vocabulary performance, and controllable generation.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 newly connects the existing one-token classifier evaluations to sparse CTMC transitions under factorized processes. This adds a mechanism explanation; interpretations of the experimental results and their existing qualifications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, architecture and training settings, hardware information, preprocessing instructions, and code/data links are retained. Experimental Details is renumbered from Appendix C to D without substantive disclosure changes.

R1.justification: v2 describes Nisonoff et al. (2024) as closely related concurrent CTMC work. v3 adds an explicit claimed continuous-time equivalence and extended comparison in Appendix B, with a pointer from Section 6. The bibliography is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes clean-data notation from x0 to x, lightly edits Section 6, inserts the guidance–CTMC appendix, and reorganizes the subsequent appendix labels and cross-references. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Added displayed derivations and redistributed existing equations change the theory appendix's page composition, including the SEDD-equivalence presentation. All six figures and 37 tables retain their visual content, captions, and structure.

improvement.justification: The CTMC comparison adds useful context, but its new formal support is flawed as printed: Equation (41) makes the no-transition probability approach zero, contradicting Equation (39), and Appendix B.1 substitutes a sum for D-CFG's required product. These errors weaken mathematical reliability and outweigh the limited clarification benefits. The original methods and empirical evidence remain intact, limiting the overall decline.
